name: Knights Templar
aliases: Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon
description: Crusading military order founded in 1119 in Jerusalem, exempt from all authority but the pope; wealthy bankers, treasurers and warriors of Mythic Europe.

name: Hospitallers
aliases: Order of the Knights of Saint John
description: The Order of the Knights of Saint John, a crusading order that began as a charitable hospital for pilgrims in Jerusalem; rivals and allies of the Templars.

name: Teutonic Knights
aliases: Order of the Teutonic Knights of Saint Mary
description: German crusading order formed around 1198 from the German hospital of Saint Mary, famed for strict discipline and turning toward the pagan lands of Eastern Europe.

name: Order of Calatrava
description: Iberian military order founded in Castile in 1158 as the military branch of a Cistercian order at the fortress of Calatrava, active in the Reconquista.

name: Order of Saint Julian del Pereiro
description: Smaller Iberian military order whose formation was supported by the Calatravans.

name: Order of Avis
description: Smaller Iberian (Portuguese) military order supported by the Calatravans.

name: Order of Santiago
description: Iberian military order of Castile-Leon that followed the rule of Saint Augustine.

name: Knights of Alcantara
description: Iberian military order based in Castile-Leon.

name: Order of Saint Lazarus
description: Military order originally composed entirely of lepers, formed in 1130 in Jerusalem's leper hospital; leprous brothers of other orders must join it.

name: Order of Saint Thomas at Acre
description: Minor order formed in Acre after the Third Crusade to care for the poor and sick and bury the dead, mainly attracting English pilgrims.

name: Swordbrethren
description: German crusading order being absorbed by the Teutonic Knights.

name: Order of Dobrin
description: German crusading order being absorbed by the Teutonic Knights.

name: Dominicans
description: Religious order mentioned as beset by scandals, unlike the Templars.

name: Franciscans
description: The Friars Minor, followers of Francis of Assisi who live in poverty, humility and charity, supporting themselves by labor or begging.

name: Poor Sisters
description: Female followers of Clare, cousin of Francis, who share the life of the poorest.

name: Cistercians
description: Monastic order whose sign language the Templars adapted; the Order of Calatrava began as its military branch.

name: Benedictines
description: Monastic order whose sign language and daily routine resemble those of the Templars.

name: Assassins
description: The Ismaili sect with whom a Templar grand master negotiated in 1173; the Templars later had their envoy killed.

name: Cathars
description: Heretics targeted by the Albigensian Crusade, sometimes sheltered in Templar houses.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of Hermetic magi; Templars have little formal contact with it, though individual commanders may know of magi and covenants.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House whose magi adopt new identities; the legendary magus Rothelin came from it.

name: Quaesitors
description: Hermetic investigators who worry that Order secrets may pass to the Templars via a confrater archmage.

name: Angevins
description: Noble family claiming the throne of Jerusalem, close to the Templars.

name: Lusignan family
description: Noble family ruling Cyprus and claiming the throne of Jerusalem, in conflict with the Templars.

name: Flagellant movement
description: Movement of pious Christians who publicly flagellated themselves expecting the Last Judgement, in which Templars later become prominent.

name: Ministeriales
description: Class of unfree German knights bound to the German king, from which most Teutons come.

name: Genoese
description: Genoese merchants supported by the Hospitallers.

name: Venetians
description: Venetian merchants supported by the Templars.

name: False Gods
description: Demonic beings who covet stolen wealth and target Templar storehouses.

name: Hugh of Payns
description: Founder and first Grand Master of the Templars (1119-1136); visited London in 1128.

name: Godfrey of St-Omer
description: One of the nine founding knights of the Templars with Hugh of Payns.

name: Bernard of Clairvaux
description: Influential churchman instrumental in gaining acceptance of the Templars.

name: Pope Innocent II
description: Pope who issued the bull Omne datum optimum granting Templar privileges.

name: Pope Innocent III
description: Pope whose planning for the Fifth Crusade was realized after his death in 1216.

name: Pope Honorius III
description: Pope who directed the Fifth Crusade and sent financial aid via Templars; Grand Master Peter reportedly has little regard for him.

name: Andrew of Hungary
description: Crusade leader of the Fifth Crusade; also referenced as Hungarian King Andrew II who granted the Teutons lands in Transylvania.

name: Leopold of Austria
description: Leader of the Fifth Crusade.

name: Pope Eugenius III
description: Pope who granted Templars the red cross and issued Milites Dei in 1145.

name: King Louis of France
description: King who led the Second Crusade; Templars took over command by Antioch.

name: Robert of Sabloel
description: Grand Master (1191-1193), formerly King Richard's admiral.

name: King Richard of England
description: Crusader king who captured Cyprus and Acre and raised Robert of Sabloel to grand master.

name: Guy of Lusignan
description: Erstwhile King of Jerusalem who bought Cyprus from the Templars.

name: Simon of Montefort
description: Leader of the Albigensian Crusade.

name: Pope Celestine II
description: Pope who proclaimed Milites Templi in 1144.

name: Henry II
description: English king for whom Templars maintained castles.

name: Thomas Becket
description: Archbishop persuaded by Templars to accept the Constitutions of Clarendon.

name: King John
description: English king advised by Aymeric of St. Maur to sign Magna Carta.

name: Aymeric of St. Maur
description: English Templar commander (1200-1220), envoy to King John; ordered construction of a massive mill in London.

name: King Henry III
description: Young English king whose treasury the Templars maintain in 1220.

name: Alan Marcell
description: English Templar commander from 1220, chief advisor to Henry III and ally of Peter of Montaigu.

name: Robert of Craon
description: Grand Master of the Templars (1136-1149).

name: Everard of Barres
description: Grand Master (1149-1152), retired.

name: Bernard of Trémélay
description: Grand Master (1152-1153).

name: Andrew of Montbard
description: Grand Master (1153-1156).

name: Bertrand of Blanquefort
description: Grand Master (1156-1169).

name: Philip of Nablus
description: Grand Master (1169-1171), retired.

name: Odo of Saint-Amand
description: Grand Master (1171-1179).

name: Arnold of Torroja
description: Grand Master (1180-1184).

name: Gérard of Ridefort
description: Grand Master (1185-1189).

name: Gilbert Erail
description: Grand Master (1194-1200).

name: Philip of Plessiez
description: Grand Master (1201-1209).

name: William of Chartres
description: Grand Master (1210-1219) whose death led to Peter of Montaigu's election.

name: Peter of Montaigu
description: Grand Master of the Templars from 1219, elected at Damietta; rumored to seek independence even from the pope.

name: Richard of Hastings
description: English Templar commander (1160-1171).

name: Richard Mallebeench
description: English Templar commander (1172-1180).

name: Geoffrey Fitz Stephen
description: English Templar commander (1180-1185).

name: William of Newenham
description: English Templar commander (1185-1200).

name: Thomas Beard
description: English Templar commander in 1200.

name: King Philip II
description: French king whose treasury is kept by the Paris Temple.

name: Brother Haimard
description: Treasurer of the French Templars and the French Crown; plots to create wealth using Hermetic magic.

name: Queen Ingebourg
description: French queen whose will Haimard will execute.

name: Oliver of Paderborn
description: Templar commander of the delegation seeking magical aid for the Fifth Crusade.

name: Afonso, Count of Boulogne
description: Noble who will overthrow Sancho II of Portugal.

name: King Sancho II
description: King of Portugal (1223-1245).

name: Martim Martins
description: Templar commander of Portugal, childhood friend of Sancho II.

name: Ramon Berengeur II
description: Count of Barcelona and Marquis of Provence who became a Templar confrere and gave them Granyena.

name: King Alfonso I
description: Aragonese king whose death brought the Templars great lands.

name: King James I of Aragon
description: King of Aragon (1213-1276) who will campaign in the Balearics and Valencia.

name: Stephen of Belmonte
description: Templar commander in Aragon seeking Hermetic magi for magical weapons and ships.

name: Hugh of Forcalquier
description: Hospitaller commander in Aragon, close to King James.

name: Frederick II Hohenstaufen
description: Holy Roman Emperor with cordial but tense relations with the Templars.

name: Brother Bonvicino
description: Papal chamberlain and Templar who will lead the flagellant movement.

name: Saladin
description: Muslim leader who recaptured Jerusalem.

name: James of Vitry
description: Bishop of Acre (1216-1228), close Templar ally.

name: Bohemond, Count of Tripoli
description: Reclaimed Antioch in 1219; supported by the Templars.

name: Leon of Armenia
description: Armenian ruler who declared war on the Templars in 1211.

name: Stephan of Tusculum
description: Ruthless Templar brother-sergeant leading a tomb-raiding team hunting relics in Greece.

name: Wido of Cornelly
description: Burgundian leper knight around whom the Order of Saint Lazarus formed.

name: Peter of Roches
description: Bishop of Winchester who will reform the Order of Saint Thomas in 1228.

name: Rothelin
description: Legendary Tytalus magus who converted, contracted leprosy and joined the Order of Saint Lazarus.

name: Guerin of Montaigu
description: Brother of Peter of Montaigu and Grand Master of the Hospitallers.

name: Eustorage
description: Uncle of Peter of Montaigu, Archbishop of Nicosia.

name: Bernard, Bishop of Puy
description: Uncle of Peter of Montaigu.

name: Nicholas
description: Retired Templar miser who hoards his stipend to donate back to the order.

name: Saint Euphemia of Chalcedon
description: Martyr venerated by the Templars; her heart and body are kept at Castle Pilgrim.

name: Virgin Mary
description: Patron of the Templars, venerated at chapter meetings.

name: Saint Ursula of Cologne
description: Saint whose silver-covered skull is kept at the Paris Temple.

name: Saint Polycarp
description: Saint whose relics sanctify Templar woolen cords.

name: William of Tyre
description: Chronicler who reported the Templar dealings with the Assassins in 1173.

name: Francis of Assisi
description: Merchant's son of Assisi whose response to God's call founded the Friars Minor.

name: Clare
description: Cousin of Francis whose followers are the Poor Sisters.

name: Patriarch of Jerusalem
description: Prelate before whom the first Templars took vows; authenticated relics.

name: Christ
description: Relics of Christ's blood and objects he used are held by the Templars.

name: Jerusalem
description: Holy City where the Templars were founded; lost to Saladin.

name: Temple of Solomon
description: Site on Temple Mount granted to the first Templars, source of their name.

name: Troyes
description: Site of the Council of Troyes where the Templars received their rule.

name: Egypt
description: Seat of Muslim power targeted by the Fifth Crusade.

name: Acre
description: Port on the bay of Haifa, Templar headquarters and central chapterhouse since 1191.

name: Damietta
description: City captured by the Fifth Crusade, where Peter of Montaigu was elected.

name: Cyprus
description: Island bought by the Templars from King Richard, ruled by the Lusignans.

name: Constantinople
description: Byzantine capital captured in the Fourth Crusade.

name: London
description: Site of the New Temple and a major Western commandery.

name: New Temple
description: Templar chapterhouse in London on the Thames, seat of the English Master.

name: Runnymede
description: Where Magna Carta was signed.

name: Paris Temple
description: Templar house in Paris serving as the French royal treasury, holding Saint Ursula's skull.

name: Tomar
description: Portuguese town founded by the Templars, with their chapterhouse at castle Cera.

name: Cera
description: Castle above Tomar, main Portuguese Templar chapterhouse.

name: Soure
description: Site of a major Templar fortress in Portugal.

name: Pombal
description: Site of a major Templar fortress in Portugal.

name: Granyena
description: Castle given to the Templars by Ramon Berengeur II.

name: Barberà
description: Castle donated to the Templars in Aragon.

name: Monzón
description: Templar castle in Aragon.

name: Montjoy
description: Templar castle in Aragon.

name: Miravet
description: Significant Western Templar commandery in Aragon.

name: Aragon
description: Iberian kingdom where Templars have been present since 1130.

name: Portugal
description: Iberian kingdom where Templars received their earliest Iberian donations.

name: Catalonia
description: Region housing many Templar sisters and consoeurs.

name: Iberia
description: Peninsula of the Reconquista.

name: Antioch
description: City reclaimed by Bohemond in 1219.

name: Krak de Chevaliers
description: Fortress granted to the Hospitallers around 1144.

name: Castle Pilgrim
description: Templar castle at Athlit housing Saint Euphemia's relics.

name: River Belus
description: River in Acre where Templar and Hospitaller mills compete for water.

name: Calatrava
description: Fortress in Castile where the Order of Calatrava was founded.

name: Culmerland
description: Territory given to the Teutons by Frederick II.

name: Transylvanian Alps
description: Holdings granted to the Teutons in 1211.

name: Templeštejn
description: Future Templar preceptory in Moravia.

name: Čejkovice
description: Future Templar preceptory in Moravia.

name: Tempelburg
description: Future Templar site in Prussia.

name: Łuków
description: Future Templar site in Prussia.

name: Esztergom
description: Future Templar site in Hungary.

name: Egyházasfalu
description: Future Templar site in Hungary.

name: Assisi
description: Italian town where Francis lived.

name: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
description: Church whose dome appears on the grand master's seal.

name: Church of the Blessed Mary of Nazareth
description: Church whose pillars sanctify Templar woolen cords.

name: Holy Land
description: Region of the crusader states and Templar activity.

name: Kingdom of Jerusalem
description: Crusader kingdom whose throne is disputed.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The game setting.

name: Tribunal of Thebes
description: Hermetic Tribunal where Templar tomb-raiders compete with Seekers.

name: La Rochelle
description: Western town with Templar holdings.

name: Armenia
description: Kingdom in conflict with the Templars.

name: Omne datum optimum
description: Papal bull of 1139 by Innocent II exempting the Templars from all but papal authority and granting them their own priests.

name: Milites Templi
description: Bull proclaimed by Celestine II in 1144 describing Templars as defenders of pilgrims.

name: Milites Dei
description: Bull of Eugenius III in 1145 clarifying Templar clergy rights.

name: Magna Carta
description: Charter signed by King John at Runnymede on Aymeric's advice.

name: Constitutions of Clarendon
description: Accepted by Thomas Becket at Templar persuasion.

name: Templar Rule
description: The strict rule governing Templar organization, hierarchy, penances and tactics, in seven sections.

name: Beauseant
description: The sacred black and white Templar banner; while raised no Templar may retreat.

name: Grand Master's Seal
description: Double-sided seal and Divine relic with Faith Score 1 granting Divine Might 10 and protection against gluttony.

name: Seal of the Templar Master of England
description: Seal bearing the Agnus Dei.

name: Sword of Tytalus
description: Legendary Hermetic heirloom said possessed by Rothelin.

name: Crown of Thorns
description: Relic displayed flowering in the grand master's hands every Holy Thursday.

name: Bathtub Cross
description: Bronze cross made from Christ's bathtub, which heals and brings rain.

name: Footwashing Bowl Cross
description: Cross made from the bronze bowl Christ used to wash the apostles' feet.

name: Phial of Christ's Blood
description: Crystal phial containing Christ's blood, authenticated by the Patriarch of Jerusalem.

name: True Cross
description: Fragments held by the Templars.

name: Woolen Cords
description: Templar cords worn as a belt, believed sacred and granting strength of will to remain chaste.

name: Templar Ciphers
description: Encryption ledgers protecting Templar communications, kept secretly in provincial commanderies.

name: Letter of Credit
description: Templar banking instrument allowing pilgrims to deposit wealth and retrieve it elsewhere.

name: Fifth Crusade
description: Crusade (1217-1221) targeting Egypt.

name: Second Crusade
description: Crusade (1147-1149) in which Templars took leading roles.

name: Third Crusade
description: Crusade (1187-1192) following the loss at Hattin.

name: Fourth Crusade
description: Crusade (1202-1204) that captured Constantinople.

name: Albigensian Crusade
description: Crusade (1209-1229) against the Cathars in which Templars stayed neutral.

name: First Crusade
description: Crusade before which the Hospitallers began.

name: Reconquista
description: Christian reconquest of Iberia supported by the Templars.

name: Battle of Hattin
description: Humiliating Christian defeat leading to the loss of Jerusalem.

name: Council of Troyes
description: Council where the Templars officially received their rule.

name: Third Lateran Council
description: Council of 1179 where bishops accused Templars of abuses.

name: Baillia
description: Revenue districts of English Templar holdings.

name: General Chapter
description: Secret decision-making meetings of the Templars held in Acre.

name: College of 13
description: Electoral body of 13 that chooses a Templar grand master.

name: Grand Master
description: Supreme leader of the Templars, elected for life, with Holy Influence.

name: Grand Commander
description: Great official second only to the grand master, carrying the beauseant.

name: Marshal
description: Chief military commander of the Templars.

name: Draper
description: Great official responsible for clothing.

name: Commander of the Land of Jerusalem
description: Templar treasurer responsible for the storehouse in Acre.

name: Master on This Side of the Sea
description: Officer sometimes appointed to oversee Western provinces.

name: Turcopolier
description: Official responsible for mercenary cavalry and brother-sergeants.

name: Gonfanier
description: Banner-bearer of the Templars.

name: Infirmarer
description: Chief surgeon of the Templars.

name: Commander of the Knights
description: Commander over the brother-knights under the marshal.

name: Under-Marshal
description: Brother-sergeant supporting the marshal.

name: Commanding Aura
description: Virtue bestowed on the grand master, granting Magic Resistance 10.

name: Divine Elections
description: Procedure for electing a grand master.

name: Trained Group Combat
description: Rule letting Templars who train a season fight as a trained group.

name: Calling on God's Aid
description: Templar practice of calling God's aid before battle.

name: Templar Sign Language
description: Limited hand signal language of the Templars.

name: Templar Prisons
description: Secret Templar prisons across Mythic Europe.

name: Petitioning
description: Clerical activity; Templar clergy petition commanders, grand master or pope.

name: Holy Influence
description: Spiritual power the grand master may exercise as a priest.

name: Code of Hermes
description: Hermetic law raised by Templar requests for magical aid.

name: Final Twilight
description: State that an archmage approaches before becoming a confrater.

name: Vis
description: Magical resource harvested from mythic sites in England.

name: Magic Resistance

name: Divine Might

name: Faith Score

name: Magic Aura

name: Hermetic Seekers

name: Novices

name: Dominion

name: Divine

name: Guardian Angels
